function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑look “calendar” of some of the most widely‑publicized festivals happening in the United States in the coming weeks and months.  (All dates are for 2026 unless otherwise noted.)  If you’re looking for a particular type of festival—music, food, cultural, arts, etc.—just let me know and I can narrow the list down for you.

| # | Festival | Date(s) | Location | Type | Highlights | Website |
|---|----------|---------|----------|------|------------|---------|
| 1 | **New York City Pride Parade & Festival** | **June 12–13, 2026** | New York, NY | LGBTQ+ Pride | Parade, live music, drag shows, vendor booths, community booths | [nycpride.org](https://www.nycpride.org) |
| 2 | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | **April 14–16 & April 21–23, 2026** | Indio, CA | Music & Arts | Headliners (rock, pop, hip‑hop), art installations, fashion, food trucks | [coachella.com](https://www.coachella.com) |
| 3 | **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 9–12, 2026** | Manchester, TN | Music & Arts | Multi‑genre lineup, art installations, yoga, food & drink | [bonnaroo.com](https://www.bonnaroo.com) |
| 4 | **Lollapalooza Chicago** | **August 4–7, 2026** | Chicago, IL | Music | Indie, rock, hip‑hop, electronic, comedy, food | [lollapalooza.com](https://www.lollapalooza.com) |
| 5 | **Summerfest** | **July 15–18, 2026** | Milwaukee, WI | Music & Family | 80+ stages, 400+ acts, food & craft beer, kids’ zone | [summerfest.com](https://www.summerfest.com) |
| 6 | **Taste of Chicago** | **August 12–14, 2026** | Chicago, IL | Food & Culture | 200+ restaurants, live music, cooking demos, kids’ activities | [tasteofchicago.com](https://www.tasteofchicago.com) |
| 7 | **South by Southwest (SXSW)** | **March 11–20, 2026** | Austin, TX | Film, Music, Interactive | Film premieres, music showcases, tech talks, networking | [sxsw.com](https://www.sxsw.com) |
| 8 | **Newport Folk Festival** | **July 28–31, 2026** | Newport, RI | Folk Music | Acoustic performances, workshops, jam sessions | [newportfolk.com](https://www.newportfolk.com) |
| 9 | **Sundance Film Festival** | **January 20–30, 2026** | Park City, UT | Film | Premieres, panels, industry networking | [sundance.org](https://www.sundance.org) |
|10 | **Burning Man** | **August 27–September 4, 2026** | Black Rock Desert, NV | Art & Community | Large-scale art installations, participatory culture, music | [burningman.org](https://www.burningman.org) |

### How to Pick the Right Festival

| What you’re after | Suggested festival(s) |
|-------------------|-----------------------|
| **Music lovers** | Coachella, Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza, Summerfest |
| **Foodies** | Taste of Chicago, South by Southwest (food + music) |
| **Film buffs** | Sundance, SXSW |
| **Family‑friendly** | Summerfest, Newport Folk Festival |
| **Art & culture** | Burning Man, Coachella (art installations) |
| **Community & pride** | NYC Pride Parade & Festival |

### Quick Tips

1. **Tickets** – Most festivals sell tickets online months in advance. Check the official site for early‑bird pricing and bundle options (e.g., multi‑day passes, VIP upgrades).
2. **Travel & Accommodation** – Book flights and hotels early; many festivals are in popular tourist destinations and fill up fast.
3. **Packing** – Bring essentials: comfortable shoes, sunscreen, reusable water bottle, rain poncho (weather can be unpredictable), and a small backpack for day‑time gear.
4. **COVID‑19 & Safety** – Check each festival’s health & safety guidelines. Some may still require masks or proof of vaccination, especially if they’re indoors or have large crowds.
5. **Local Events** – Many cities host smaller, local festivals around the same time. Check city tourism sites for additional options.

---

#### Want More Details?

If you’d like deeper information on a specific festival—lineup, schedule, ticket tiers, travel tips, or even a comparison of a few festivals—just let me know!
